SELECTED_INDEX: 7  
CONFIDENCE: 0.25  
EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by two very strong low-frequency bands at 554 cm⁻¹ and 644 cm⁻¹ – a region characteristic of P–S / P–F stretches in phosphoryl difluorothioethers.  A medium-strong band at 1017 cm⁻¹ matches the typical ν(P–O) (or P–F deformation) mode of O=PF₂-containing molecules, and the 1294 cm⁻¹ band fits the ν(P═O) stretch (rule GFQ-024 states O=PX₃ gives ~1290 cm⁻¹).  Additional weaker bands at 720–790 cm⁻¹ correspond well to P–F stretches (PF₅ equatorial ν ≈ 740–950 cm⁻¹, rule GFQ-042).  The high-wavenumber region (2900–3005 cm⁻¹) shows only aliphatic C–H stretches, consistent with the single ethyl group in CCSP(=O)(F)F and the absence of O–H or N–H stretches.  Among the candidates only molecule 7 (CCSP(=O)(F)F) possesses a phosphoryl (P═O), two P–F bonds and a P–S linkage that can simultaneously account for the very strong 554/644 cm⁻¹ doublet, the 1017 cm⁻¹ band and the 1294 cm⁻¹ ν(P═O).
